clinicalPearls: Caused by biallelic loss-of-function variants in TCAP, encoding telethonin (T-cap), a small Z-disc protein that caps the N-terminus of titin and stabilises the sarcomere.
Distinctive phenotype combines proximal limb-girdle weakness with unusually early distal lower-limb involvement, notably anterior tibial weakness and foot drop.
Onset is typically in childhood to early adulthood with slowly progressive pelvic- and shoulder-girdle weakness.
First and most extensively characterised in Brazilian kindreds; it remains one of the rarer recessive limb-girdle subtypes worldwide.
Creatine kinase is usually moderately raised.
Muscle biopsy characteristically shows rimmed vacuoles, and immunolabelling demonstrates absent telethonin.
Cardiac surveillance is warranted because dilated cardiomyopathy has been reported in a subset of patients.
Either calf hypertrophy or distal lower-limb atrophy may be observed on examination.
reference.pathophysiology: Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy R7 is a recessive skeletal-muscle disorder caused by biallelic loss-of-function variants in TCAP on chromosome 17q12, which encodes telethonin (also called T-cap), a small titin-cap protein of the sarcomeric Z-disc. Telethonin is phosphorylated by the titin kinase domain and binds the N-terminal Z-disc region of titin, anchoring the thin filaments and contributing to sarcomere assembly, mechanical stability and stretch-sensing signalling. Pathogenic frameshift and nonsense variants (classically first identified in Brazilian families) abolish telethonin expression, so the Z-disc loses its cap, sarcomeres become mechanically unstable during repeated contraction, and progressive myofibre degeneration with rimmed-vacuole formation ensues. Because telethonin is also expressed in cardiac muscle, a proportion of patients develop dilated cardiomyopathy, which helps distinguish this subtype from several other recessive limb-girdle dystrophies.
additionalDifferentials: Distal myopathies such as tibial muscular dystrophy
GNE myopathy (distal weakness with rimmed vacuoles)
additionalInvestigations: Next-generation sequencing gene panel or whole-exome sequencing including TCAP
Muscle MRI to map the pattern of selective muscle involvement
Electromyography and nerve conduction studies (myopathic pattern; exclude neuropathy)
ECG and echocardiography for cardiac surveillance
Respiratory function testing when weakness is advanced
redFlags: New breathlessness, orthopnoea or ankle oedema suggesting cardiomyopathy
Frequent falls related to foot drop with risk of injury
Symptoms of nocturnal hypoventilation such as morning headache and unrefreshing sleep
reference.prognosis: Progression is slow and ambulation is often retained well into adulthood, although loss of walking can occur over time. Prognosis is chiefly modified by the presence and severity of cardiac involvement.
pitfalls: Prominent distal weakness may cause misclassification as a distal myopathy or a peripheral neuropathy.
Rimmed vacuoles can be misattributed to sporadic inclusion body myositis.
Reduced telethonin staining may be secondary in other conditions, so genetic confirmation is essential.
Its rarity outside Brazilian populations means the diagnosis is frequently overlooked.
references: Consensus classification of the limb-girdle muscular dystrophies
management: No disease-specific pharmacotherapy exists; management is supportive within a specialist neuromuscular multidisciplinary team
Ankle-foot orthoses for the characteristic anterior tibial weakness and foot drop, with physiotherapy to maintain gait and prevent contractures
Occupational therapy and mobility aids to preserve independence as pelvic- and shoulder-girdle weakness progresses
Cardiac surveillance with ECG and echocardiography, since cardiac involvement is the principal modifier of prognosis in this subtype
Respiratory function monitoring with spirometry and non-invasive ventilation if hypoventilation develops
Genetic counselling and family screening given autosomal recessive inheritance
